title: He was the wrong man to set free.
paragraphs: He was the wrong man to set free.

A criminal.
A rebel.
A man whose name was stained with violence and blood.
And yet… when the moment came, the crowd didn’t hesitate.

Not the healer.
Not the sinless One.
Not Jesus.

And if we’re honest—
we would’ve been standing there too.
Because this isn’t just his story.

📖 “Now Barabbas was a robber.” — John 18:40
📖 “Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas!” — Luke 23:18

That shout?
It wasn’t just a crowd.
It was humanity choosing sin over Savior.
And here’s the part that hits deeper than comfort can carry…

Barabbas didn’t plead innocence.
He didn’t argue his case.
He didn’t earn his freedom.
The innocent Son of God stood silent while the guilty man walked free.
📖 “He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He opened not His mouth.” — Isaiah 53:7
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because what happened that day wasn’t a mistake of justice.
It was the design of redemption.
📖 “But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Call it “mistakes.”
Call it “bad decisions.”
Call it “just being human.”
But Scripture doesn’t whisper about sin—it exposes it.
📖 “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

Chains loosen.
The door opens.
And the verdict changes.

Not because we became good—
but because Jesus became the substitute.
📖 “He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree.” — 1 Peter 2:24
Do you understand what that means?

Every hidden sin.
Every secret addiction.
Every shame you bury in silence—
The cross wasn’t just wood and nails.
📖 “He was pierced for our transgressions… and by His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
But here’s the question that won’t leave you alone:
What did Barabbas do after he walked free?
And maybe that silence is intentional.
Because now the spotlight turns to you.

Will you go back to the same life?
The same chains?
The same sin that almost destroyed you?
And follow the One who took your place?
📖 “If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.” — Matthew 16:24
Jesus didn’t die so you could stay the same.
He died so you could be transformed.

New heart.
New life.
New identity.
📖 “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
But we don’t have to live like prisoners anymore.
And the Savior who took your place?
📖 “He is not here, for He has risen, as He said.” — Matthew 28:6
This is Jesus offering you the same freedom Barabbas walked into—

A relationship.
A purpose.
A future anchored in eternity.
Receive what you could never earn.
📖 “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.” — Acts 16:31
If this convicted you… don’t ignore it.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
